bittel-scope-classical-optimization: Section I, p.1: the authors state they focus on the second challenge, the classical optimization over the circuit parameters. Read in context after the two-challenge sentence.
bittel-scope-figure1-classical-part: Figure 1 caption, p.1: the caption states the work addresses the complexity of the classical optimization part. Matches Section I.
bittel-scope-graphs-considered: Section I B, p.2: 'Throughout, we consider only adjacency matrices A of undirected, unweighted graphs with at least one edge', with the matrix form given.
bittel-convention-exponential-precision: Section II, p.2: the paper adopts the convention that a minimization is solved when solved to exponential precision, and says it uses it throughout. The paper's own convention.
bittel-problem2-continuous-maxcut: Problem 2, p.2: instance, task and the function mu(phi) of Eq. 1 are defined in the paper.
bittel-lemma1-problem2-np-hard: Lemma 1, p.3: stated and proved on the same page by reducing to {0,pi}^d (Eqs. 2 to 4) and a many-one reduction from MaxCut. The text layer prints 'P != NP' as 'P = NP' (the manifest notes this; page 1 render shows the not-equal sign), so the quote's condition is intact. MaxCut NP-hardness is textbook background.
bittel-lemma1-discrete-minima: Proof of Lemma 1, p.3: derived from Eq. 2 (dependence on one coordinate is a cosine) and Eq. 3; the conclusion that continuous output can be made discrete in polynomial time is stated in the proof.
bittel-problem3-oracular-setup: Problem 3, Section III A, p.3: instance, oracle and task defined; the paper states the oracle's purpose (capture only the classical optimization effort).
bittel-oracle-postselection: Section III A, p.3: the authors describe how their own oracle is to be read (postselection, deterministic return). It is a statement about the paper's own model, attributed to the authors in the value. Basis is setup, not a result.
bittel-proposition1-oracular-hardness: Proposition 1, p.4: stated with its assumption (P != NP, glyph lost in text layer) and proved by reduction from Problem 2 with O of Eq. 6 and generators sigma_y/2 (Eqs. 6 to 8); the expectation equals mu(phi).
bittel-error-decomposition: Section III A, p.4, Eqs. 11 and 12: the paper defines delta as model mismatch plus optimization error, with the two terms described.
bittel-definition1-optimization-error: Definition 1, p.4: stated in the paper with Eq. 13.
bittel-corollary1-no-error-below-one: Corollary 1, p.4: stated with its P != NP condition and proved in the text by Eqs. 14 to 18 (boosting to Delta >= 1 - alpha^k). The final step is terse and uses that alpha < 1 for MaxCut (APX-hardness, background in Section II), but the proof is in the paper.
bittel-boosting-technique: Proof of Corollary 1, p.4: the paper's own construction (Eqs. 15 and 16, k copies on k x d qubits); the poly(d) terms for constant k follows directly from the product form. A construction the paper defines, not a result proved elsewhere.
bittel-log-qubits-setup: Section III B, p.5: the paper states the regime N in O(log d) and that the Hilbert space then has polynomial dimension so expectation values and ground state are efficiently computable (immediate from dimension 2^N).
bittel-problem4-vqa-minimization: Problem 4, p.5: defined in the paper.
bittel-theorem1-vqa-np-hard: Theorem 1, p.5: proved by explicit many-one reduction (Eqs. 19 to 24). I checked Eq. 24 on the rendered page: the s,p sums give (1/8)A(cos(phi_i - phi_j) + cos(phi_i + phi_j) - 2) = mu(phi).
bittel-corollary2-decision-np-complete: Corollary 2, p.5: membership in NP is argued from polynomial-time evaluation with phi as certificate (real-valued, covered by the paper's exponential precision convention, Section II) and hardness from Theorem 1. The proof is short but in the paper; the setting (polynomial dimension) is stated.
bittel-theorem2-single-layer: Theorem 2, p.6: single generator H = sum E_j(...) gives O(phi) = mu(E phi) exactly (Eqs. 28 and 29); Lemma 2 energies make E phi reach any phase vector within epsilon, and Lemma 1 gives hardness. Short, but proved in the paper from its own lemmas.
bittel-problem6-qaoa-setup: Problem 6, p.6: instance, state and task defined in the paper, with L in unary (footnote 1).
bittel-limit-theorem3-precision: Section III C, p.7: the authors state that their Theorem 3 construction has Hb energies over many orders of magnitude, so it needs an incredibly precise device. A limit of their own construction (consistent with E_i = 2 pi / m^i).
bittel-theorem4-qaoa-small-norms: Theorem 4, p.7 with Appendix B, p.8 to 10: the main text calls it an outline, but Appendix B gives the full construction (B1 to B6), the state (B7, B8), the expectation lower bound (B9) and the equivalence to mu(beta - pi/2). Restriction ||Hb||, ||Hc|| <= 3 is stated. I read the rendered pages 9 and 10. The Orest >= 0 step is asserted but follows from the block structure.
bittel-appendixb-construction-layers: Appendix B, p.9: the paper states its own construction, a many-one reduction from Problem 2 with L = d layers and the Hilbert space K of dimension d x d x 2 x 2 in 2d+1 blocks.
bittel-appendixb-norm-bounds: Appendix B, p.10: norms ||Hgs|| = 3, ||HT(kappa)|| = 2, ||HT|| = 1, ||Hp|| = 1, so ||Hc|| = 1 and ||Hb|| = 3 (rendered page confirms the norm bars). Stated as 'direct calculations'; they follow from the definitions (B1 to B6) and the eigenvalues listed on p.9.
bittel-limit-no-boosting-for-qaoa: Section III C, p.7: 'Here, we are unable to use the same boosting technique to increase the hardness result further.' A limit the authors state on their own method.
bittel-gaussian-state-definition: Section III D, p.7: the paper defines a Gaussian state as one arbitrarily well approximated by a thermal state of a quadratic Hamiltonian.
bittel-problem7-free-fermions: Problem 7, p.7: instance and task defined in the paper, with Eqs. 36 and 37 giving the observables and ground state.
bittel-theorem5-free-fermions-np-hard: Theorem 5, p.7 to 8: stated with 'even if rho_0 is pure' and proved by explicit reduction (Eqs. 38 to 41) using the covariance matrix Gamma = 1/(2d) from (C13); the result equals mu(phi) as in Eq. 24. Appendix C supplies the free-fermion identities.
bittel-theorem5-encoding-size: Proof of Theorem 5, p.8: the paper states its construction uses n = 2d fermionic modes and L = d layers.

theory_low.bittel-local-minima-discrete-set: p.3: a remark after Eq. 5. The derivative and Hessian are given, but the claim that a point is a local minimum 'whenever changing any single phi_i increases the objective' is argued informally. It mixes the discrete flip test with the second-order condition and is not proved. The claim is not stated as a lemma.
theory_low.bittel-lemma2-ergodic-spectra: Lemma 2, p.5 to 6 and Appendix A, p.8 to 9: the lemma is proved in Appendix A (E_i = 2 pi / m^i, epsilon = 4 pi / m; rendered page 5 confirms). The value misstates the formula as '2 pi to the power of m times i' and does not give epsilon, so it does not match the passage. The bit-precision remark n x log2(m) is asserted, not shown. A corrected value would be HIGH on proved result.
theory_low.bittel-corollary3-time-evolution: Corollary 3, p.6: stated loosely ('a system with logarithmically many qubits... starting from some initial state') and justified by one sentence viewing Theorem 2 as time evolution. The value also holds the authors' novelty claim ('unaware of this statement being explicitly proven before'), which is the authors' claim. Graded by the weaker.
theory_low.bittel-theorem3-qaoa-single-layer: Theorem 3, p.6 to 7: a reduction is given, but the key step is informal: 'for tau << 1 the contribution of g becomes insignificant', with gamma = pi/(2 tau). No bound shows the extra 2 tau cos sin g term leaves the minimizer of f unchanged, and scaling E_i into |E_i| < 1 is not worked out.
theory_low.bittel-corollary4-qaoa-optimization-erro: Corollary 4, p.7: the quotes drop the inequality and the P != NP condition (they sit in typeset equations and in the proof). The proof, Eq. 35, rests on Theorem 4's Hc_min and on alpha_max, the best MaxCut approximation ratio, whose value is cited and conditional (Section II), not proved here. Not settled by the quoted passage.
theory_low.bittel-gradient-methods-error-bound: Section III C, p.7: a one-sentence consequence of Corollary 4 with alpha = 1/2. That ratio comes from the informal p.3 argument that any local minimum can be a gradient method's result, plus a cited ratio. Not proved in the paper.
theory_low.bittel-appendixc-time-evolution-second-m: Appendix C, p.10: the derivation (C1 to C3) is in the paper, but the appendix limits it to 'the special case of particle number preserving Hamiltonians'. The value says 'for free fermion Hamiltonians' and drops that condition. Overstates the passage. A value with the condition would be HIGH on proved result.
